pr_title: Change account search to match by text when opted-in
pr_body: I took over this branch https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/pull/24663 which fixes https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/issues/13272. I had to deal a bit with merge conflicts from https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/pull/24716. Note: In order to get this to work I had to run `bundle exec rake chewy:update` This PR tries to let searching by bios work, but only when the user is opt-ed in. It also does not allow for a bio search to happen in a post. It only happens in the search bar. Here are a bunch of screen shots of me testing this locally. Anne -- You can see that Anne has `foo` in her bio. Carol -- So does Carol, but Carol should not be found for searches. A search for `foo` -- You can see that Anne and the hashtag and a post with `foo` all come up. (that post is by this `any_user`). Note that I am searching for `foo` and not `#foo` because a search that contains the string `#` only will search the tags index. This, I think, should be changed in a future PR, but I hear the case that it could be done in this one. A post with `@Anne` -- You can see that searching for `anne` in a post still works. But a post with `@foo` doesn't work -- My assumption here is that `SearchService` is only used by the search bar and not on posts. As far as I could tell this was true, but if this is wrong I would love to be told so.
pr_comments: A few mocks in the test suite need to be updated with the new argument.
This doesn't seem to work in the field. Details here: https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/issues/13272#issuecomment-1615937514

I was under the mistaken impression, that this hashtag search was a work-around for the (I think) majority of instances where ElasticSearch is not enabled, but instead @ClearlyClaire [reports that it requires ElasticSearch](https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/issues/13272#issuecomment-1623101307). If this is true, _shudder of frustration_.

More proactively:

1. Those of us who value being found need a resource listing instances where we can be found using Mastodon's native search tools. Which apparently means an instance list that shows ElasticSearch preferences.
2. If a feature does nothing, an empty search results bar is an unacceptable UI piece. Instead, we need a message like this one indicating "Searching biographies by their content, or by hashtags is not enabled on this Mastodon server." (Something I [pleaded for and received for search in general here](https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/issues/18218#issuecomment-1364729583).)
3. Let's perhaps reopen this issue so that this can be implemented without ElasticSearch in the future. 
4. Can we clearly document the conditions when this hashtag search function works: Is it functional within instance A (if ES is enabled), for users on instance A searching for connected instances (where ES is enabled on A), for users on instance A searching for connected instances (only if ES is enabled on A and the target instance B)?

issue_context.title: Search in Bio and meta-fields.
issue_context.body:
When searching for a keyword, and that keyword is mentioned in someone's public *bio*, or in one of the "meta fields" as key of value, the account should be returned as search result.

### Pitch

We can search for toots, and for usernames and even for keywords in the usernames@instance.tld strings. But we cannot search for the contents of the (public) bio or metadata fields.

Given Anne at example.com, a user with a public, listed Bio that says `Working at #foo, lover of Bar. Significant other of @bob@example.social`.  
Given Carol at example.com, a user with a account set to *not listed*, with bio `Working on #foo`.  
And given Bob at example.social followed by @anne@example.com with bio `Significant other of @anne@example.com`.

When any user on example.com searches for the term "example.social", currently already Bob shows up.

And when any user on example.com searches for the term "Bar" Anne should show up. 
And when a user searches for `#foo` any toot with hashtag `#foo` *as well as* Anne should show up. 
But when searching for `#foo` Carol should not show up.

### Motivation

This would benefit finding users. E.g. one could search for people advertising they are working on something, share a hobby, have the same interests and so on. 

This would allow new users to find interesting accounts to follow faster.

This would make the bio and meta-fields more usefull and a make accounts a more interesting unit: currently they are not searchable and only accounts are listed.

This might be an advanced feature, that is only available if an instance has chewy/Elasticsearch enabled.

I'm willing to develop this, but need to know whether this is wanted and how this would work in more detail before I can do so.
comments:
Please do this as soon as possible. As I've observed at https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/issues/18128#issuecomment-1114026909

- The inability to search profiles is profoundly maddening. If the first word of my profile is "anthropologist" and I don't turn up on a search for "anthropologist" (honestly, preferrably also for "anthropology"), what in the world is my profile for?
this is a very temporary fix, but if anyone finds this thread and just wants to do this now, you may use this python script. https://gist.github.com/d3cline/c31beed644f1da87c7c7f427fbca5419

So grateful for the work being done on this. However, despite mastodon.online being run on nightly builds and popping up a user interface cue that this feature is activated, it doesn't seem to actually find profiles. I've tried #Mastodon, #Rstats, #history as well as the example below and retrieve zero results each time. I can't be sure of others, but my "Suggest account to others" box is checked in preferences. Search bar cue for searching profiles works… Zero results despite visible matching hashtag in my profile…
This hasn't been deployed on mastodon.online yet (which is using a nightly from a few days ago)

@ClearlyClaire can I ask a couple of details about how precisely this'll work?
1. Which profile fields will be searched, will it be name, bio and featured hashtags?
2. Will searches work across multiple fields? As in, if 'cycling' is in my bio, and someone searched for "Brendan cycling", would my profile be returned?
3. Will word searches also return matching hashtags listed in the bio or featured hashtags? As in, if I had #cycling in my bio, would searching for 'cycling' return my profile?
Ah, mastodon.online does not have Elasticsearch (the text search service) enabled if I remember correctly.

review_comments: It’s a way to future proof against having to completely recreate the index when adding more filtering capabilities.

Since this drops any reference to `acct`, I'm worried this would disadvantage auto-completion of remote user mentions when you start typing their full handle, e.g. `@gargron@ma` should match `@gargron@mastodon.social` rather than `@gargron@fake.server`
It’s just a field rename. Username is still both username and domain.
Ah, right, I missed that! Not sure why the definition doesn't simply reuse `acct` or `pretty_act` though.

I can't really comment on this as I am not knowledgeable in Chewy or ElasticSearch. That being said, this seems very tailored to English and I worry this could provide subpar results in other languages.
It’s a copy of the analyzer we use for posts.

I'm not sure what it's supposed to be used for, but having a `verified` value that does not reference the value of the exact verified field does not seem useful, surfacing that the account has a verified link, without showing which, may be misleading.
It can be useful to exclude results that have no verification at all, however.
I'm not sure I understand the use case
